mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q01.stem: Someone proposes fixing one button of a two-hand control and operating only the other. What hazard explanation is appropriate?
options: An emergency stop makes two-hand operation unnecessary.
Faster starting prevents entanglement.
The machine may operate with the freed hand in the danger area.
People behind the machine face no hazard.
reasons: An emergency stop does not replace guarding or operating conditions.
Speed does not prevent entry into a hazard area.
Fixing one button removes the condition keeping both hands at the controls.
Approaching third parties may also be crushed.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q02.stem: A drawing has phantom lines for another position of a moving part and hatching for a section. Which explanation is appropriate?
options: Phantom lines indicate motion positions; hatching indicates section areas.
Every phantom line indicates dimensional tolerance.
Machine both as solid outlines.
Hatching always indicates electrical continuity.
reasons: Distinguish their purposes when reading drawing information.
Read tolerances from separate dimension specifications.
Their purposes differ from visible outlines.
Hatching indicates sections or specified areas, not electrical continuity.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q03.stem: An automatic-return pushbutton and maintained emergency-stop actuator were assumed identical. What should be reassessed?
options: A round shape always returns automatically.
Contact shape certifies the entire machine’s safety.
Erase identifiers and use order to identify them.
Check holding and release conditions against symbols and specifications.
reasons: Shape alone does not establish return behavior.
Whole-system safety is not established by contact shape.
Identifiers and specifications are needed to identify behavior.
Actuation and return require separate checks.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q04.stem: Under equal length, area and temperature, textbook resistivities are1/58 for annealed copper and1/35 for aluminum. Which is correct?
options: Aluminum’s low mass necessarily means lower resistivity.
Annealed copper has lower resistivity in this comparison.
Density and resistivity are identical quantities.
1/58 is larger, so copper resistance is larger.
reasons: Low mass and conductivity are separate properties.
Resistance is proportional to resistivity under equal conditions.
Density relates mass to volume.
The fractions are reversed in magnitude:1/58 is smaller.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q05.stem: A nonmetal plate’s drawing specifies a flat washer, but none is in the parts box. What should you do?
options: Ignore part-number differences if the screw head fits.
Do not omit it; verify configuration and supply before tightening.
Double torque to compensate.
A spring washer always eliminates the flat washer.
reasons: Head fit alone does not establish conformity.
Do not change the specified assembly independently.
Excess torque does not replace a missing washer.
The two washers’ roles and specifications differ.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q06.stem: When a feed handle was reversed, play created a range over which motion was not transmitted. What is this play called?
options: Surface roughness
Thread pitch
Feed speed
Backlash
reasons: Roughness is fine surface unevenness, not feed play.
Pitch is the axial distance between corresponding points on adjacent threads, not mechanism play.
Feed speed is movement per time, not a play dimension.
Reversal play in motion transmission is backlash.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q07.stem: A screw advances0.5 mm per turn and its thimble has50 divisions. What is one division?
options: 0.5 mm
25 mm
reasons: This divides by10 rather than50.
0.5 mm is the whole turn’s advance.
Multiplying0.5×50 does not divide the turn.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q08.stem: You see tsunami hazard-zone and tsunami evacuation-site signs. Which interpretation is appropriate?
options: Ignore restrictions for a brief stay despite a hazard sign.
Both indicate only safe assembly points.
Distinguish hazard information from evacuation guidance and check the route.
Choose by color without reading.
reasons: A short stay does not justify ignoring hazard information.
A hazard zone is not the same as a safe refuge.
Compare sign purpose and disaster type.
Read the subject and guidance, not just color.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q09.stem: Halving the long side of420×594 mm A2 producesA3. What size isA3?
reasons: This isA4 after another halving.
This is unchangedA2.
This isA1, one size larger.
594/2=297 paired with420.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q10.stem: To distinguish lampL, ammeterA and fuse in a circuit, what should be checked?
options: Decide functions solely from round physical shapes.
Compare symbols with the legend and separate indication, measurement and protection.
An ammeter always replaces fuse protection.
Nearby symbols always have the same function.
reasons: Physical shape and schematic symbols convey different information.
Identify each symbol and function separately.
A measuring instrument does not unconditionally replace protection.
Diagram distance does not establish identical function.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q11.stem: A nut driver is prepared for a small hex nut. What is appropriate?
options: Use the same tip for every hex-socket bolt.
Compensate for a loose fit with force.
Check the tip fits across flats and the working space.
Select only by the nominal thread diameter.
reasons: Hex sockets need a suitable hex key.
Loose tools may damage corners.
Compare holding and tool dimensions.
The tool fits nut width across flats.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q12.stem: What is appropriate in the textbook square-hole method using drilled holes, cutting and filing?
options: Leave allowance inside the outline, clamp and finish progressively.
Drill outside the outline and fill later.
Cut beyond the marked line to avoid finishing.
No clamping is needed if the tool fits.
reasons: Preserve retained geometry and manage finishing allowance.
Removing outside material loses required stock.
Excess cutting does not restore required geometry.
An unclamped workpiece can move dangerously.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q01.stem: Electrolytic and ceramic capacitors have equal capacitance. Which judgment is sound?
options: Equal capacitance always means interchangeability.
Also compare polarity, voltage, temperature and frequency.
Every capacitor has the same dielectric.
Similar shape eliminates rating-document checks.
reasons: Capacitance is only one condition, not the whole specification.
Judge suitability with construction and operating conditions.
Dielectrics include oxide films and ceramics.
Shape does not establish polarity or ratings.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q02.stem: Connect100Ω and200Ω in series to an ideal6 V source. What is voltage across100Ω?
options: 3 V
4 V
6 V
2 V
reasons: Different resistances do not divide voltage equally.
4 V is across200Ω.
This is not parallel connection applying full voltage to each.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q03.stem: How are roles divided between a contactor and thermal overload relay in a combined starter?
options: The contactor switches load; the thermal relay detects overload.
The thermal relay alone directly interrupts all main-circuit current.
Thermal operation is independent of current and duration.
The contactor alone supplies every short-circuit protection function.
reasons: These are the two distinct magnetic-starter roles.
This confuses detection with main-circuit interruption.
Thermal overload detection depends on current and time.
Verify short-circuit protection separately.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q04.stem: You want star-delta starting to reduce current. Which selection approach is appropriate?
options: Ignore winding terminals and ratings.
Reduced current always increases starting torque.
Also compare winding compatibility, load torque and protection.
Starting current alone proves suitability for every load.
reasons: Compatible winding connections and ratings are prerequisites.
Current reduction does not mean torque increase.
Check equipment and load conditions together.
Starting torque and other conditions are also necessary.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q05.stem: A product requires weight and strength checks but has passed only dimensional inspection. What is appropriate?
options: Also perform specified weight and strength checks for structural requirements.
One successful operation eliminates structural records.
Correct length automatically passes weight.
Certify strength from appearance color.
reasons: Meet each inspection’s target separately.
Function does not replace structure or records.
Dimensions and mass are separate quantities.
Color is not a strength-test result.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q06.stem: Injection molding is considered for a small batch of identical resin products. Which comparison is appropriate?
options: Use the same mold for different products without conditions.
Compare initial mold cost separately from processing time per item.
Ignore all tooling cost in unit cost.
Mass-production suitability makes it cheapest at every quantity.
reasons: Molds are designed for product shape and flow.
Compare initial and quantity-dependent costs.
Ignoring it prevents total-cost comparison.
The allocated initial cost varies with volume.

options: 100 nm
reasons: 0.1 mm is less than1 mm, not ten million nm.
100 nm is1000 times too small using1 mm=10⁶nm.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q08.stem: How should grease penetration and grade-number magnitudes be read?
options: Every larger number means softer in the same direction.
Read it as exactly the same quantity as oil viscosity.
The scale name is unnecessary if colors match.
Check scale name and specified standard before interpreting magnitude.
reasons: Different scales relate numbers to hardness differently.
Consistency and oil viscosity are different measured quantities.
Color cannot identify the scale or suitability.
Do not confuse penetration-value direction with grade-number direction.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q09.stem: Compare proportional lines withV horizontally andI vertically. What does a greater slope indicate?
options: Changing axes leaves slope meaning unchanged.
Every straight line means resistance is temperature-invariant.
Lower resistance under the same conditions.
Higher resistance under the same conditions.
reasons: Swapping axes reverses numerator and denominator.
Temperature and other assumptions apply.
I/V=1/R, so greater slope means smallerR.
Resistance is the reciprocal of this slope.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q10.stem: A basic electromagnetic-relay holding circuit is replaced by aPLC with retention settings. What should happen?
options: Recheck power-restoration and restart conditions in the actual settings.
The same name eliminates restoration checks.
Omit all stop-input checks.
The word holding guarantees every safety condition.
reasons: Check actual circuits and settings, not just names.
Holding design can change restoration behavior.
Stop conditions remain necessary functional checks.
Safety includes faults and restoration conditions.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q11.stem: Which description fits inflating resin with air?
options: Every FRP uses only this method.
Every cured resin remelts freely.
It is always lathe machining.
It is the basic idea of blow molding.
reasons: FRP also uses impregnation and lay-up.
Cross-linked thermosets cannot remelt in the same way.
A lathe rotates and cuts workpieces.
Distinguish air inflation from injection molding.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-14-q12.stem: You are comparing circuit-forming photosensitive film and finished-board solder resist. Which understanding is correct?
options: A metal base permits direct continuity between conductors and base metal.
Distinguish process and role and check applicable instructions.
Every material called film has the same material and process.
Legend printing eliminates the need to form copper conductors.
reasons: Check the structure and specifications, including insulation.
Photosensitive film, protective film and markings serve different purposes.
Distinguish process and material requirements.
Legend printing is marking, not a substitute for required conductors.
